rich_summary: Markandeya recounts the cosmic origin of a famous conflict. After the dissolution of the universe into a single ocean, Vishnu sleeps upon the serpent Sesha. From the lotus springing from his navel arises Brahma. Two powerful demons, Madhu and Kaitabha, appear and threaten Brahma, waking Vishnu. Through clever speech Vishnu secures from them a promise that they will grant him a boon; he then asks to slay them. Bound by their vow, they only request to die on an uncovered place and to become his sons. Finding no uncovered spot in the flooded cosmos, Vishnu places them on his own thighs and decapitates them. Their son Dhundhu later performs terrible austerities and gains near‑invulnerability from Brahma, then begins tormenting the worlds. The sage Utanka and King Kuvalaswa—empowered by Vishnu—march to confront the menace, setting the stage for Dhundhu’s destruction.

highlight_spans.why: The opening cosmic dissolution sets the mythic scale and frames the story within the cycle of creation and destruction.
The iconic image of Vishnu sleeping on Sesha and the lotus arising from his navel, from which Brahma is born.
The clever exchange where Vishnu secures the demons’ promise and asks the boon that he be allowed to slay them.
The moment Vishnu discovers his uncovered thighs and uses them as the place to fulfill the condition before killing Madhu and Kaitabha.
Introduction of Dhundhu, son of the slain demons, whose asceticism and boon from Brahma drive the next major conflict.

top_scenes.scene_text: Vishnu sleeping upon the vast serpent Sesha on the cosmic ocean while a radiant lotus rises from his navel with Brahma seated upon it.
Vishnu lifting the demons Madhu and Kaitabha onto his bare thighs and severing their heads with the blazing discus amid the primeval waters.
King Kuvalaswa marching with his thousands of sons across the desert of sands as gods gather in the sky and shower flowers before the coming battle with Dhundhu.
